title: Psalm 23: The Lord Is My Shepherd

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Hello, and welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 13]

Find a way to lie down that feels easy. Pull the covers up. Let your phone rest somewhere you will not have to reach for it. [pause 15]

Tonight we are reading the twenty-third Psalm, slowly, twice. It may be the most loved psalm there is. Many people learned it as children, and many have heard it at the bedside of someone they love. [pause 15]

You do not have to do anything but listen. [pause 15]

verses.text: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
The psalm begins with one small word. My. [pause 19]

Not a shepherd somewhere far away. My shepherd. David had been a shepherd boy. He knew what it was to count the sheep at night, to find water for them, to carry the one that was hurt. [pause 20]

A shepherd does not ask the sheep to find the pasture on their own. He leads. He goes first. [pause 20]

Notice that the psalm does not pretend there is no dark valley. It says yea, though I walk through it. The valley is real. But so is the one who walks it with you. [pause 24]

Here are two more short passages to sit beside it. [pause 18]

verses.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.
I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Lie down in peace, and sleep. That is a line you can borrow tonight. [pause 20]

And the good shepherd, Jesus said, gives his life for the sheep. He does not leave when the night comes. [pause 20]

And Isaiah pictures the shepherd carrying the lambs close to his chest, leading gently those with young. Gently. That is how he leads you tonight. [pause 22]

Now we will read the twenty-third Psalm once more. This time, you might let it be a little slower in your mind. Let each line land before the next one comes. [pause 24]

verses.text: A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life: and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Now let the words go quiet. [pause 8]

You do not have to hold on to them. They will be there in the morning. [pause 10]

Let your shoulders drop. Let your hands open. Let the bed hold the weight of you. [pause 12]

If a worry comes back, you can hand it over again. As many times as it takes. [pause 12]

The night is long and quiet, and you are not alone in it. [pause 15]

Feel the quiet of the room. The small sounds. The dark. Nothing is asked of you here. [pause 20]

You are held, the psalm said. You are known. You are kept. [pause 20]

Rest now. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Every psalm and companion is stored KJV pasted by code; reflections paraphrase in short echoes (no 8+ word typed scripture) and stay with each psalm's own point (shepherd, evening rest, keeping, shelter, stillness, quiet soul, being known, waiting, a shield in flight, light and waiting). No promise of sleep or protection: Psalm 91 says plainly it does not promise nothing hard will happen; Proverbs 3:24 framed as 'not a promise for every night'. God never quoted in first person outside scripture. Headings (Ps 3, Absalom) used only as the text's own titles.

cultural.note: Plain, unhurried English a tired woman at 11 PM can follow; no filler, no church jargon unexplained; hospital and grief named gently; shared rests vary their wording so the close is not the same sentence every night; pacing tuned only by silence (pauses) to 13.5-13.7 min voiced at the measured 117 wpm.
